title: Local bounds for the relative tensor homology of a perfect complex
statement: Let X,Y be schemes [def-pc-scheme] with Y Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and let f:X→Y be locally of finite type and stalkwise of finite Tor dimension [def-pc-perfect-morphism]. Let E in D(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category] be perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Fix a complex K representing E, a K-flat complex P of f⁻¹O_Y-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex], and a quasi-isomorphism q:P→K restricted along f⁻¹O_Y→O_X [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. For each x in X there exist an open neighbourhood U containing x and integers a≤b such that, for every f⁻¹O_Y-module sheaf F, every degree i<a or b<i, and every y in U, the underlying abelian-group stalk at y of H^i(Tot(P tensor F[0])) is zero. X need not be quasi-compact; the bound is uniform on U and for all F.

source.place: Tags 069C ((3) implies (2)) and 0B6G (condition (3)); Cohomology Tag 09U9; online text https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/069C and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B6G

proof.text: A locally finite type morphism to a Noetherian scheme is pseudo-coherent. Tag 069C applies to the stalkwise hypothesis [def-pc-perfect-morphism], giving around each point an open neighbourhood on which the structure sheaf has Tor amplitude [-d,0] over the inverse-image structure sheaf. Its proof uses a finite polynomial presentation, pseudo-coherence over that polynomial ring, and the finite global dimension of its fibres to turn stalkwise perfectness into perfectness on an open neighbourhood. This is the essential geometric step; no compactness is assumed.

proof.text: Intersect that neighbourhood with a strictly perfect neighbourhood for E [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Choose [r,s] containing the degrees of the bounded model. Each term is a retract of a finite free structure module and therefore has Tor amplitude [-d,0] after scalar restriction. The finite filtration by terms, with quotients the terms shifted into their respective degrees, gives amplitude [r-d,s] for the entire complex by the long exact sequences of tensor cohomology. Enlarge the endpoints if necessary so the interval is ordered. The neighbourhood and interval are independent of the test module.

source.place: Tags 069C ((3) implies (2)) and 0B6G (condition (3)); Cohomology Tag 09U9; online text https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/069C and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B6G

proof.text: The prescribed quasi-isomorphism q from K-flat P [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] computes the scalar-restricted derived tensor of K, hence that of E through the given representative isomorphism. Apply the K-flat stalk criterion [lem-pc-kflat-stalk-criterion] to the ringed space (X,f⁻¹O_Y) to obtain K-flat stalk complexes. At each stalk, compare to a common K-flat replacement of the scalar-restricted bounded model. K-flat model independence [lem-pc-kflat-tensor-quasi-iso] (transported from the one-point-site module presentation), exactness of restriction and stalks, and stalk compatibility with total tensor identify its tensor homology stalks with those of the local bounded model. They therefore vanish in every degree outside the chosen interval. For a zero local model use [0,0]; an empty scheme has no points to check.

theorem perfect_relativeTensor_locally_bounded
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (hperfect : HasStalkwiseFiniteTorDimension f)
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory X) (hE : IsPerfect X E)
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (e : Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K ≅ E))
    (P : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj
        (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageRing f.base Y.sheaf))) ℤ)
    (hP : CochainComplex.IsKFlat (R := TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageRing f.base Y.sheaf) P)
    (q : P ⟶ ((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars
      ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).map
          (Modules.tensorPullbackRingMap f))).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K) (hq : QuasiIso q) :
    ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧
      ∀ F : SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose
          (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
          (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj
            (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageRing f.base Y.sheaf)),
        ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → ∀ y : X, y ∈ U →
          IsZero ((TopCat.Sheaf.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u} X.carrier ⋙
            TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} y).obj
              ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj
                ((CochainComplex.mapBifunctor P
                  ((HomologicalComplex.single _ (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj F)
                  (@MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor _ _ (SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory
                    (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageRing f.base Y.sheaf)))).homology i)))
